entry.title: GKR protocol with a machine-checked core and a faster sparse prover with identical proofs
entry.summary: GKR with a Machine-Checked Core, and a Sparse Prover Made Faster with Byte-Identical Proofs ethresear.ch · Nov 8, 2026This post describes StateSync-GKR, which gives the first machine-checked soundness bound for GKR on general layered circuits, in Isabelle/HOL. The bound is applied to a soundness proof for sparse-Merkle updates. Release 1.2 of the sparse prover proves 2.41 to 2.71 times faster and produces byte-identical proofs.

entry.title: How large can EIP-8141's validation budget be? A mempool DoS benchmark
entry.summary: How large can EIP-8141's validation budget be? A mempool DoS benchmark ethresear.ch · Nov 7, 2026A technical discussion on the Ethereum Research forum by the Nethermind team. It notes that EIP-8141 caps unpaid validation gas at 100k, which is too low for privacy transfers and post-quantum signatures. The authors simulate a denial-of-service attack on a Nethermind node, flooding it with transactions that use the full validation budget and then fail, at caps from 100k to 500k. They report that with an in-client protection that pauses transaction validation during block processing, a cap of 300k is viable.

entry.title: A privacy pool on frame transactions: which parts work and which do not yet
entry.summary: A privacy pool on frame transactions: what works, and the case that does not yet ethresear.ch · Nov 6, 2026Nethermind researchers built a privacy pool using BN254 Groth16 proofs on frame transactions, where the pool itself pays gas so private withdrawals need no relayer. They report a withdrawal costs 679,322 gas on a test node. Two problems remain open: the proof check exceeds the EIP-8141 validation gas cap, and a pool cannot pay for calls made from the user's own address.

entry.title: TULIP: A permissionless decentralized identity concept
entry.summary: TULIP: Permissionless Decentralized Identity Delving Bitcoin · Nov 6, 2026The author proposes a pseudonymous identity system that avoids central coordinators and uses the Bitcoin blockchain as the timestamping and ordering authority for identity key changes. Keys rotate through a precommitted Taproot chain, keeping the onchain footprint small. A linked whitepaper, Tuliproot, also suggests a 4-byte witness header to help index important state-change transactions.

entry.title: Walraswap: an equilibrium-based decentralized exchange that integrates external AMM liquidity
entry.summary: Walraswap: equilibrium-based decentralized exchange integrating external AMM liquidity ethresear.ch · Nov 6, 2026This paper presents Walraswap, a decentralized exchange design based on equilibrium theory for exchange economies, which settles batches of trade orders together and can incorporate external AMM liquidity. The authors argue that equilibrium requires uniform clearing prices and inclusion of all available orders, and they propose governance by a DAO that elects solvers, with public order flow to discourage censorship. The paper also presents theoretical results on the existence, uniqueness of net trades, and computation via convex optimization.

entry.title: Question about direct messaging on the forum
entry.summary: Direct Messages (DMs) Delving Bitcoin · Nov 3, 2026A poster on the Bitcoin protocol development forum says they want to contact user @neonrooks to request their npub. They have added the artist's song "Off the Chain" to btcplaylist.com and want listeners to be able to zap the artist. Unable to find a direct message option on the forum, they raised the question in this thread.

entry.title: Full OP_RETURN value pruning for satd Bitcoin nodes
entry.summary: Full OP_RETURN value pruning Delving Bitcoin · Nov 3, 2026The satd Bitcoin node implementation adds an optional feature to prune OP_RETURN output values from on-disk block files using hole-punching. It is controlled by options such as -pruneopreturn, -pruneopreturnsize and -restoreopreturns. The author argues this lets operators express preferences without breaking consensus, but notes disk usage may increase rather than decrease and that pruned nodes cannot serve some block data.

entry.title: Storage-optimized replay protection: packed flag lanes versus per-flag booleans, and whether the protocol could offer cheaper storage.
entry.summary: Storage-optimized replay protection: from hash => bool to packed flag lanes, and can the protocol offer better? ethresear.ch · Nov 3, 2026The post covers protocols that must permanently record one small flag per event, such as privacy-pool nullifiers and unordered nonces. It compares three layouts: one boolean per flag, a 256-flag bitmap word, and per-party lanes within a word, with gas estimates for each. The author argues that packing can only approach fixed cost floors, and asks whether the execution layer could offer replay flags directly at a price suited to that use.

entry.title: Why searchers and builders favor candle auctions and what it means for the post-Glamsterdam builder market
entry.summary: Why searchers and builders like candle auctions (and why it matters for the builder market post-Glamsterdam) ethresear.ch · Nov 2, 2026This Ethereum Research forum post models auctions with a random end time and few participants, showing that open-bid "candle" auctions can yield higher bidder profits than sealed-bid auctions. The author argues this outcome arises as an equilibrium of the one-shot game, without explicit coordination or collusion. The post links this to frequent bid updating and discusses implications for ePBS and sealed bidding.

entry.title: SEACAST: A Fast, Lean Broadcast Protocol for Ethereum With an Executable Spec and Formal Model
entry.summary: SEACAST: fast, lean, sampled broadcast for Ethereum, with an executable spec and a formal model ethresear.ch · Oct 22, 2026The author proposes SEACAST, a protocol for quickly delivering large Ethereum messages. Nodes forward chunks as they arrive, and coding and sampling let each node receive only the parts it needs. The post reports that on 50 Mbps networks SEACAST is faster and uses fewer bytes than ECBroadcast and gossipsub, and it comes with an executable specification and a formal model. Correction Nov 2, 2026: Link to the original updated

entry.title: Machine-checked proof that BIP340 batch verification stays sound with 128-bit derived randomizers
entry.summary: Machine-checked soundness of BIP340 batch verification with 128-bit derived randomizers Delving Bitcoin · Nov 2, 2026The author used Lean 4 with Mathlib and VCVio to machine-check the soundness of BIP340 batch verification when its randomizers are shrunk to 128 bits and derived deterministically. The proof covers independent uniform randomizers, randomizers hashed from the whole batch, and incremental derivation. In the random-oracle model the forgery bound is (q+1)/2^128, but deterministic derivation allows offline grinding, where about 2^64 hashes get an invalid batch accepted with probability around 2^-64.

entry.title: Scaling Trust: EIP-8288 on OP Stack for Post-Quantum Signatures
entry.summary: It's time to scale the trust: EIP-8288 on OP Stack ethresear.ch · Nov 2, 2026An Ethereum Research forum discussion proposes EIP-8288 to move L2 transaction signatures and proofs out of transaction data and post one aggregate proof covering many blocks to L1. The author estimates that with leanSPHINCS signatures, transactions compress to 100 to 129 bytes, needing about 2.8 to 3.3 blobs per L1 block instead of about 79 without aggregation.

entry.title: Asset-level spending limits and recovery: should rate limiting live in the asset rather than the account?
entry.summary: Asset-level spending limits and recovery: should rate limiting live in the asset rather than the account? ethresear.ch · Nov 2, 2026This Ethereum Research forum thread proposes enforcing spending limits and key-compromise recovery at the token contract level for ERC-20s, and potentially at the protocol level for native ETH, rather than only in account code. The author argues that account-level limits can be bypassed through existing token allowances or by re-delegating under EIP-7702. The proposal sketches rolling-window limits, a 14-day delay on security-weakening changes, an irreversible compromised state, and a pre-registered recovery address, and invites feedback.

entry.title: "Snowball to Snowstorm": A Forum Post Sharing a Paper on Mempool Soft-Agreement Protocols
entry.summary: Snowball to Snowstorm Delving Bitcoin · Nov 2, 2026A community member on Delving Bitcoin shares a paper describing a protocol that reaches soft agreement on mempool transactions before a block is found. It combines several pre-existing protocols and is somewhat Snowball-like, but operates over entire groups of transactions rather than individual ones. The post says the goal is significantly faster block propagation and better machine utilization.

entry.title: ERC Draft: Account Authority Lifecycle for STVA
entry.summary: ERC draft: Account Authority Lifecycle for STVA ethresear.ch · Nov 1, 2026This draft proposes a standard model and interface covering the full lifecycle of authority over an account, including issuance, activation, attenuation, review, suspension, revocation, and recovery. It aims to prevent stale owners, modules, or keys from retaining authority beyond their intended purpose. High-risk authority changes must pass independent simulation and be authorized through Scoped Capability Tokens.

entry.title: Eltoo state chain on signet, third build using TEMPLATEHASH, CSFS and INTERNALKEY
entry.summary: Eltoo state chain on signet, third time: TEMPLATEHASH + CSFS + INTERNALKEY Delving Bitcoin · Nov 1, 2026The author rebuilt a small Alice/Bob/Carol Eltoo state channel on signet for the third time, this version using TEMPLATEHASH, CSFS and INTERNALKEY. The run deliberately published an old state and then replaced it with a newer update. It compares update-leaf and witness sizes across APO+CTV, CSFS+CTV and TEMPLATEHASH, and argues that TEMPLATEHASH returns the template hash to the script so the update script needs only three opcodes.

entry.title: PropAMM fills on Ethereum mainnet and TEMBRI toolbox support: same-block quotes and tight spreads
entry.summary: PropAMM fills on Ethereum mainnet and PropAMM support for TEMBRI (toolbox): same-block quotes, a small spread, and flow taken from lagging AMMs ethresear.ch · Nov 1, 2026The post analyses 92,627 fills across nine Ethereum PropAMMs, on-chain venues priced by a single maker, over 30 days from 10 September to 9 October 2026. Three venues accept quotes only when stamped with the current block's timestamp, so every fill executes against an update in the same block. Takers paid about 0.45 bp at the fill, and prices did not move in their favour afterwards.

entry.title: ERC Draft: Independent Simulation Result (STVA)
entry.summary: ERC draft: Independent Simulation Result for (STVA) ethresear.ch · Oct 31, 2026This draft proposes a canonical, content-addressed format for simulation results that any independent party, such as a wallet, hardware device, or third-party verifier, can regenerate and re-verify from the same inputs and state snapshot. It aims to make simulation a reproducible, machine-checkable artifact rather than a result that depends on trusting a frontend service. The results can be bound into signatures and capability tokens.

entry.title: Scoped Capability Tokens for STVA
entry.summary: Scoped Capability Tokens for STVA ethresear.ch · Oct 30, 2026This proposal defines short-lived, purpose-limited, revocable authorization tokens based on EIP-712 typed data or ERC-1271-compatible signatures. Each token grants only specific actions, such as upgrading an implementation, transferring tokens, or installing a module. Tokens include fields such as issuer, subject, scope hash, validity window, salt, and optional simulation or intent hashes, and can be verified before signing. The draft also outlines Basic, Standard, and Strict compliance levels and discusses on-chain versus off-chain revocation.

entry.title: Post-quantum signatureless authorization using recursive zero-knowledge proofs
entry.summary: Post-quantum signatureless authorization with recursive verification ethresear.ch · Oct 30, 2026This forum post proposes a post-quantum authorization scheme that replaces digital signatures. An authority publishes a commitment to a reusable secret, and each action is authorized by a freshly randomized zero-knowledge proof bound to the requested action. It describes a quantum security reduction, a binary-field implementation, and recursive composition with execution proofs.
